sam.w: fyi onboarding mariscope9b (int4) — seeing a repeating phase-lattice / "corrugation" pattern in attention-derived embeddings after quant. repro and quick numbers below. :eyes:

sam.w: repro steps:
```
# bench vm
python tools/onboard_eval.py --model mariscope9b --quant int4 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --dump-embeds --seed 123
```

sam.w: metrics: f16 top1=0.792, int8=0.789, int4=0.602; mean cosine f16 vs int4 = 0.59. heatmaps show alternating bands every 256 tokens, and PCA frames show a lattice-like fold.

anya: can you paste exact export flags? which rotary config (shared/headwise)? proj packing? ln-fold? tokenizer/version?

sam.w: exporter: rdw-quant-v2 with flags `--mode=int4 --scheme=asym --proj-order=packed-qkv --clip=dynamic` ; rotary left as shared; no ln-fold; tokenizer bpe-nfkc-v2025-07.

ciro: packed-qkv + shared-rotary = classic risk. packed proj mixes q/k scales; with int4 small quant noise can produce phase-wrapping that looks like a lattice. try re-export: headwise rotary + qkv-serial. also try disabling packed qkv to see if behavior is tied to packing.

maya: also try tiny freq edits: `rotary.freq_scale=0.995` and `1.005` — small shifts sometimes move the freq out of a wrap boundary. and check ln-fold on/off because folding can change per-proj dynamic range and push different clip bins.

sam.w: quick tokenizer sanity check done — token ids match across builds for samples. not a tokenization drift.

bench-bot: run 1735551240 started; artifacts will land in s3://redwood-qa/mariscope/onboard/1735551240/ when complete.

eva: also rule out KV cache steady-state: run with `--kv-warmup 0` and `--kv-warmup 256` and a no-batch accumulation run. cache reuse can amplify small rotary phase errors into visible bands for long ctx.

ciro: if re-export helps but residual persists, do a micro-bisect: dump per-head rotary cos/sin tables for float16 and int4 and compute phase offset per head and per position. plot headwise phase delta; if certain head-groups saturate, we can try per-head clipping or asymmetric buckets.

sam.w: starting a small grid: {rotary.headwise: true,false} x {proj-order: packed,serial} x {freq_scale: 0.995,1.0,1.005} x {ln-fold true,false} x {kv-warmup 0,256}. will stream first numbers.

sam.w: initial quick update: headwise + qkv-serial + freq_scale=1.0 + ln-fold=false -> int4 top1 0.72, mean cosine 0.78. lattice amplitude reduced but still visible > 2048.

maya: big delta — that points to proj mixing + shared-rotary amplifying quant noise. for the longctx residual, ensure converter wrote rotary freqs with shape [heads, L] not [L] incorrectly broadcast; we've seen a converter bug tile freqs and create periodic artifacts at scale.

eva: also consider running quant with per-channel clipping on proj weights (headwise clipping) or per-head scaling before quant to balance dynamic ranges. int4 is sensitive to heterogenous ranges across packed tensors.

ciro: another experiment: export int4 but use a small calibration set with sequence lengths matching your worst-case longctx (e.g., 4096) — calibration-run mismatch can leave tails that only show up at long positions.

sam.w: good points. i'll attach per-head dumps and PCA frames after the runs. thanks team — will update when plots upload. :thumbsup:
